objectives.description: Run deploy-headless.sh, capture stdout+stderr to deploy-output.txt

objectives.note: Deploy output is 4 lines: acquired lock, 'Resynced 6 extension(s)', verify pointer. No explicit 'preserved (settings install-once)' narrative line appeared in deploy-headless.sh's own output (that phrasing belongs to init.lua's unload/reload path, not the deploy script) -- install-once preservation was instead confirmed directly by checking settings.json content post-deploy (objective 4).

objectives.description: Confirm settings.json not overwritten (lean-lsp still present)
objectives.note: grep -n lean-lsp .claude/settings.json hits at line 33 (byte-position shifted from pre-deploy's 188). Investigated: jq -S canonicalization of current .claude/settings.json vs settings.json.bak (the pre-deploy copy) is byte-identical (diff exit 0) -- the file is semantically unchanged, only raw key ordering differs (top-level 'permissions' block moved position; hooks array entries reordered). This is NOT deploy-headless.sh rewriting the install-once file (its copy-skip logic was independently confirmed by presence of the still-live grant); most likely the Claude Code harness itself rewrote settings.json (e.g. on session start/stop) between the Phase 1 backup and now, independent of the deploy. Confirms install-once mechanism behaved as documented: content, not byte-layout, is preserved.
